question: Why is the breathing rate of aquatic organisms much faster than the terrestrial ones?

options.text: Because of more O2 in water
Because of less CO2 in water
Because of less O2 in water

solution:
The correct answer is __**Because of less O2 in water**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The breathing rate of aquatic organisms is much faster than that of terrestrial organisms primarily because there is **less O₂ in water**,

 
 
• necessitating quicker respiration to obtain sufficient oxygen for survival.
 
 
 
• **Water holds much less dissolved oxygen (O₂)** compared to the amount of oxygen available in the atmosphere.
 
• The oxygen concentration in water can be significantly lower, especially in warmer water or in environments with high levels of organic matter.
 
• ** Aquatic organisms, such as fish and amphibians**, have adapted to extract oxygen efficiently from water.
 
• They often have** specialized respiratory structures** like gills that allow them to extract dissolved oxygen as water flows over them.
 
• To **meet their oxygen requirements i**n an environment where oxygen is less available, aquatic organisms need to respire more rapidly.
 
• This results in a** higher breathing rate compared to terrestrial organisms, which have access to more oxygen in the atmosphere.**
